982c3ec0ec53e7a7.title: Critical Integer‑Overflow in VMware Workstation/Fusion Enables Host Code Execution
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.summary: Broadcom patched CVE‑2026‑59346, a critical integer‑overflow in VMware Workstation and Fusion (versions 25H2/26H1) that lets a locally‑privileged VM user execute arbitrary code on the host via the VMXNET3 adapter. The flaw scores 9.3 CVSS and has no work‑around.
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.impact: Attackers who gain administrative rights inside a VM can break out to the hypervisor, compromising the entire host and any other VMs running on it.
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.action: Apply the VMware Workstation 26H1u1 and VMware Fusion 26H1u1 updates immediately.

0c97dcbaac2a5941.title: JetBrains Cadence Compromised via Critical TeamCity Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑63077)
0c97dcbaac2a5941.summary: Unpatched TeamCity allowed threat actors to exploit CVE‑2026‑63077, a deserialization flaw with a CVSS 9.8 score, to breach JetBrains Cadence. Attackers accessed the Cadence server, extracted AWS credentials, and copied backup data from 2024, potentially exposing current user workloads and secrets.
0c97dcbaac2a5941.impact: Security teams must treat all Cadence executions, inputs, outputs, and stored credentials as compromised, and recognize the broader risk of unpatched CI/CD tools in supply‑chain attacks.
0c97dcbaac2a5941.action: Immediately revoke or rotate all AWS and other credentials stored in Cadence and audit all Cadence workloads for malicious activity.

88d106f1bb825bd4.title: Linux kernel maintainer releases multiple stable updates fixing bugs and security issues
88d106f1bb825bd4.summary: Greg Kroah‑Hartman published eight new stable Linux kernels on September 2 (7.2.3, 7.1.13, 6.18.49, 6.12.108, 6.6.156, 6.1.187, 5.15.220, 5.10.269) and three additional releases on September 7 (7.2.4, 6.18.50, 6.12.109). Each release bundles extensive bug fixes and security patches across the tree, and 7.1.13 marks the final update for the 7.1 series.
88d106f1bb825bd4.impact: The updates close numerous vulnerabilities and stability regressions, reducing attack surface for systems running the listed kernel versions.
88d106f1bb825bd4.action: Upgrade all Linux hosts to the newest stable kernel for their series immediately.

3699d96dcf48c22c.title: Multiple Linux Distributions Release Broad Security Updates Across Core Packages
3699d96dcf48c22c.summary: All major Linux distributions released a wave of security patches this week, covering critical components such as dbus-broker, freerdp, nodejs, php, openssl, kernel, and graphics libraries. The updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Oracle Linux, and Mageia, addressing numerous vulnerabilities without referencing specific CVE identifiers.
3699d96dcf48c22c.impact: Unpatched systems remain exposed to potential remote code execution, privilege escalation, and denial‑of‑service attacks in the affected packages. The breadth of the updates means that many production environments may be vulnerable if the patches are not applied promptly.
3699d96dcf48c22c.action: Apply the latest security updates from your distribution’s package manager without delay.

dd5a568c6d3e40c6.title: Grml 2026.09 Live Distribution Released with Linux 7.1.8 Kernel and exFAT Boot Support
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.summary: Grml 2026.09, codenamed “Hättiwaritätti,” ships as a Debian‑based live distro for sysadmins, built on upcoming Debian 14 (forky). It upgrades to the Linux 7.1.8 kernel, adds native exFAT boot capability, and bundles GNU Screen 5.0.1, delivering newer hardware support without new security advisories.
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.impact: The kernel upgrade brings broader hardware compatibility and performance improvements, but introduces no immediate security patches or CVEs to address. Existing Grml deployments remain secure, but administrators should verify compatibility with their hardware and tooling.
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.action: Upgrade to Grml 2026.09 after testing boot on exFAT media and confirming kernel compatibility with critical workloads.

21263e7ebe9581a1.title: FBI Launches Investigation into Dark‑Web Service Selling 153 Million North American Driver’s Licenses
21263e7ebe9581a1.summary: A new dark‑web marketplace, Nexus, is offering digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver’s licenses, along with millions of other ID documents, sourced from a widely used identity‑verification provider in Louisiana. The FBI’s New Orleans field office has opened a formal probe into the data breach.
21263e7ebe9581a1.impact: Security teams must assume that personal identification data of millions of users has been compromised, increasing the risk of identity theft, fraud, and credential stuffing attacks. Any systems that ingest or validate driver’s license images from the implicated provider are now exposed to potential abuse.
21263e7ebe9581a1.action: Immediately audit and, if necessary, replace any third‑party identity‑verification services that source driver’s license images from the Louisiana provider, and monitor for suspicious activity involving compromised IDs.

cc32169d9af5f5da.title: Unicode‑Tag “ASCII Smuggling” Powers Massive Finance‑Themed Phishing Campaign
cc32169d9af5f5da.summary: Microsoft detected a high‑volume phishing operation that injects invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000‑U+E007F) into finance‑related keywords, splitting words like “funding” to bypass Office 365 email filters. The campaign peaked at 2.5 million messages per day in February, then fell sharply after mid‑May, but remains active.
cc32169d9af5f5da.impact: Security teams see traditional keyword‑based filters rendered ineffective against this Unicode‑based obfuscation, while Defender for Office 365 still blocks >99 % of the mail using other signals.
cc32169d9af5f5da.action: Update email security policies to include detection of Unicode tag characters and enable Microsoft Defender for Office 365’s Unicode‑smuggling signatures.

c95e648fd687a543.title: PostgreSQL Patches 12‑Year‑Old Logical Decoding Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑6471)
c95e648fd687a543.summary: PostgreSQL released updates fixing CVE‑2026‑6471, a critical 7.2‑rated flaw that lets any REPLICATION‑enabled account execute arbitrary OS‑level code via logical decoding output plugins. The bug, present since logical decoding debuted in version 9.4 (2014), is mitigated by a new whitelist parameter restricting loadable plugin libraries.
c95e648fd687a543.impact: Attackers can compromise database hosts by abusing replication users in CDC, backup, or standby setups, potentially gaining full system control.
c95e648fd687a543.action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, or 14.24 (or later) and verify the output_plugin_libraries whitelist is configured.

018c9450de11b26e.title: Ted Backdoor Embedded in Compromised HAProxy Binaries Enables Stealth Web Traffic Interception
018c9450de11b26e.summary: A custom Linux toolkit named Ted was compiled into trojanized HAProxy load balancers at two South Korean firms, allowing attackers to hijack HTTP requests, serve forged pages, and exfiltrate data via hidden C2 channels that bypass backend logs and HAProxy statistics.
018c9450de11b26e.impact: Security teams must treat HAProxy binaries as potential infection vectors, as the implant can silently intercept and modify traffic while evading traditional monitoring.
018c9450de11b26e.action: Audit all HAProxy binaries for unauthorized modifications, verify code signatures, and redeploy from trusted sources while tightening host execution controls.

d4908d4411cee4ef.title: Over 440,000 Exploit Attempts Target Critical WordPress Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE Flaws
d4908d4411cee4ef.summary: Threat actors have launched more than 440,000 exploit attempts against two critical WordPress plugin vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-14894 in Super Forms and CVE-2026-32475 in Elementor Pro—allowing unauthenticated file uploads that lead to remote code execution.
d4908d4411cee4ef.impact: These attacks can drop PHP web shells, create admin accounts, exfiltrate data, and fully compromise WordPress sites using the vulnerable plugins.
d4908d4411cee4ef.action: Update Super Forms to 6.3.314 and Elementor Pro to 4.2.2 immediately, and block malicious POST requests to admin-ajax.php.
